props.scope: when the procedure learns from interaction data

props.positive_test: acts greedily on a learned value function with no separate policy parameters

props.positive_test: parameterises the policy directly with no learned value baseline

props.positive_test: parameterises both a policy and a learned value estimate
props.negative_test: having only one of the two

props.scope: to control procedures
props.characteristic: whether the procedure acts over extended sub-behaviours

props.examples: flat, hierarchical

props.positive_test: selects one primitive action per environment step
props.negative_test: selecting a sub-policy that runs for many steps
props.examples: DQN, PPO, SAC

props.positive_test: selects temporally extended options or subgoals with their own termination
props.negative_test: selecting a primitive action each step

A.deriv.name: Information used to choose a step

props.scope: to any procedure that searches a parameter or configuration space
props.characteristic: what information a single step consumes
props.positive_test: name the value this procedure takes for: information used to choose a step
props.negative_test: a procedure with no search at all
props.examples: first-order, preconditioned, zeroth-order, closed-form, combinatorial, sampling
props.notes: multi-valued; changed from single-valued after HMC and XGBoost each needed two values cardinality=many from 64 pinning cases: genuine: TRPO is first- and second-order, PlaNet first- and zeroth-, XGBoost combinatorial and second. Phase 1 reached the same conclusion from NUTS, and the rl and opt regions independently again default=A.deriv.first: gradient descent is the unmarked case in this field. A blank means the default, so an explicit pin equal to it is redundant. SPLIT in D.1: A.deriv.fixed was added here and the pinning immediately showed it is not a sibling -- the other six answer what one step consumes, it answered what stops the loop, which is why 42 of 155 nodes came out as both. Termination is now A.loop.

props.positive_test: uses the gradient, scaled only per coordinate
props.examples: SGD, momentum, Adam, AdamW, Adafactor, Lion
props.notes: per-coordinate adaptivity is still first-order

props.positive_test: uses a matrix approximation of curvature across coordinates
props.examples: L-BFGS, K-FAC, Shampoo, Muon, Gauss-Newton, natural gradient

props.positive_test: uses only function evaluations, never derivatives
props.examples: CMA-ES, OpenAI-ES, Nelder-Mead, random search, simulated annealing

props.positive_test: obtains the solution by solving an equation or decomposition in one shot
props.negative_test: terminates only after repeating the solve to convergence -- that is a closed-form step inside a loop, so it takes A.loop.fixpoint as well
props.examples: OLS normal equations, ridge closed form, PCA by SVD, LDA, Platt-free isotonic fit
props.notes: negative test reworded: it said `iterating a step rule to convergence`, which contradicted 60 nodes that iterate a closed-form inner solve. One solve per step and a convergent outer loop are now different questions.

props.positive_test: searches a discrete structure with pruning, DP or enumeration
props.examples: branch and bound, Viterbi, beam search, Hungarian matching, greedy submodular

props.positive_test: explores by drawing from a target or proposal distribution, not by descending
props.examples: Metropolis-Hastings, Gibbs, HMC, NUTS, SMC, Langevin dynamics
props.notes: SGLD carries this and A.deriv.first

props.scope: to iterative fitting procedures

The data region found its scope predicate (`iterative fitting`) contradicts the phase-1 worked examples, which use A.cadence.full to mean `sees the whole dataset`. Needs a ruling, not a cardinality default=A.cadence.mini: minibatch is the unmarked case; full-batch and streaming are the claims. A blank means the default, so an explicit pin equal to it is redundant.

props.positive_test: each update uses the entire training set
props.examples: L-BFGS on full data, batch gradient descent, EM over the full dataset, IRLS

props.positive_test: each update uses a random subset of fixed size
props.negative_test: each update uses the full dataset or one example
props.examples: SGD, Adam, most deep learning

props.positive_test: updates after each individual example, typically without storage
props.examples: perceptron, online gradient descent, Hogwild! per-sample, online k-means

props.positive_test: each example is seen once and cannot be revisited
props.examples: streaming k-means, reservoir methods, online change-point detection, sketching

props.scope: when more than one worker participates
props.characteristic: how workers synchronise with each other
props.positive_test: name the value this procedure takes for: coordination topology
props.examples: single, centralized-sync, centralized-async, decentralized, federated-device, federated-silo

Parties are now A.parties default=A.topology.single: one process holding the whole run is the unmarked case. A blank means the default, so an explicit pin equal to it is redundant.

props.positive_test: one process holds the whole run
props.examples: default single-GPU training

props.positive_test: all workers synchronise their updates at a global barrier
props.examples: all-reduce SGD, FSDP, ZeRO, synchronous pipeline

props.positive_test: workers push to a shared aggregator without waiting for each other
props.examples: Hogwild!, Downpour, ASGD, FedBuff

props.positive_test: workers exchange only with neighbours; there is no aggregator
props.negative_test: an aggregator or all-reduce over all workers
props.examples: D-PSGD, gossip SGD, SGP

props.scope: when data originates in more than one place
props.characteristic: whether raw data may be moved to one place
props.positive_test: name the value this procedure takes for: raw-data locality constraint
props.examples: pooled, local-only
props.notes: single-valued cardinality=one: the pinning pass never needed two values here default=A.datalocality.pooled: pooled data is the unmarked case. A blank means the default, so an explicit pin equal to it is redundant.

props.positive_test: raw training data is allowed to be centralised
props.examples: standard distributed training, data-parallel pretraining

props.positive_test: only model updates or statistics cross the party boundary
props.negative_test: shipping raw examples to a central store
props.examples: federated learning, split learning, local differential privacy pipelines

props.scope: when the paper claims a protection property
props.characteristic: what adversary the guarantee is stated against
props.positive_test: name the value this procedure takes for: formal privacy or security property
props.examples: differential privacy, secure aggregation, encrypted computation, unlearning
props.notes: multi-valued cardinality=many from 2 pinning cases: genuine: secure aggregation and differential privacy are claimed together no default on purpose: an empty A.privacy means no protection is claimed

props.positive_test: a per-example sensitivity bound and a reported epsilon budget
props.examples: DP-SGD, DP-FedAvg, PATE, DP-FTRL

props.positive_test: the aggregator provably cannot see individual updates
props.negative_test: only the raw data is withheld

props.positive_test: computation proceeds on encrypted or secret-shared values

props.positive_test: provides a stated guarantee that a specific example's influence is gone

props.scope: to interactive settings

props.examples: single, cooperative, competitive, mixed

A blank means the default, so an explicit pin equal to it is redundant.

props.positive_test: one policy interacts with a stationary environment
props.examples: DQN, PPO on MuJoCo

props.positive_test: several agents share one team reward

props.positive_test: rewards are neither identical nor strictly opposed
props.negative_test: a purely cooperative or purely zero-sum setting
props.examples: sequential social dilemmas, mixed-motive MARL, negotiation agents

props.scope: to multi-agent or partially observed control
props.characteristic: what each agent can observe when acting, as opposed to when training
props.positive_test: name the value this procedure takes for: information available at execution
props.examples: centralized, CTDE, decentralized
props.notes: single-valued cardinality=one: the pinning pass never needed two values here; renamed from A.exec: it collided in meaning with the role slot R.sys (formerly R.exec) no default on purpose: the three observation modes are real claims with no unmarked case

props.positive_test: the acting policy conditions on global state at deployment
props.examples: joint-action controllers, centralized planners

props.positive_test: global information is used only during training
props.negative_test: global information is used while acting
props.examples: MADDPG, MAPPO, QMIX, COMA

props.positive_test: no global information is used at any stage
props.examples: IQL, IPPO, independent learners

props.scope: to any method whose output type is constrained
props.characteristic: the type of a single output element
props.positive_test: name the value this procedure takes for: required output or action space
props.negative_test: a method indifferent to output type
props.examples: discrete, continuous, hybrid, structured
props.notes: single-valued cardinality=many from 10 pinning cases: many UNBLOCKS but it is two questions: element type (disc/cont) and joint structure (struct). Every autoregressive model needs disc AND struct; narrowed after pinning: it was asking element type and joint structure at once, which is why every autoregressive model needed `disc` and `struct` together. Joint structure is now A.outstruct no default on purpose: discrete and continuous are a genuine choice, not a default and a deviation

props.positive_test: requires a finite enumerable set of outputs or actions
props.examples: DQN, Q-learning, top-k sampling, classification losses

props.positive_test: requires a real-valued, differentiable output or action space
props.examples: DDPG, TD3, SAC continuous, CEM-MPC, regression losses

props.positive_test: requires a mixture of discrete choice and continuous parameters
props.negative_test: a purely discrete or purely continuous space
props.examples: parameterised-action RL, hybrid action DDPG
props.notes: speculative: a thin literature

props.scope: to any procedure
props.characteristic: whether repeated application with fixed inputs gives the same result
props.positive_test: name the value this procedure takes for: determinism of the procedure's output
props.examples: deterministic, stochastic
props.notes: single-valued cardinality=many from 10 pinning cases: many is provisional. The gen region reports the positive test is unusable as written -- `any internal sampling` makes every deep run stochastic -- so 167 of its pins rest on a line the agent drew, not on the table default=A.determinism.det: deterministic is the unmarked case, and the test is too loose to rely on otherwise. A blank means the default, so an explicit pin equal to it is redundant.

props.positive_test: same inputs and same parameters always produce the same output
props.examples: greedy decoding, beam search, k-means given an initialisation, PCA

props.positive_test: the procedure samples internally, so outputs vary across seeds
props.negative_test: the only randomness is in data ordering
props.examples: top-p sampling, dropout, MCMC, Thompson sampling, diffusion sampling

props.scope: to any estimator
props.characteristic: what the procedure returns about its own uncertainty
props.positive_test: name the value this procedure takes for: treatment of estimate uncertainty
props.negative_test: a procedure that returns no estimate
props.examples: point, interval, posterior, ensemble
props.notes: single-valued cardinality=many from 42 pinning cases: many UNBLOCKS but the real defect is a conflation: A.uncert.post says `posterior over parameters or functions`, and a VAE's q(z|x) is a posterior over per-example latents. Split into what-is-returned x over-what default=A.uncert.point: a point estimate is the unmarked case; anything richer is the contribution. A blank means the default, so an explicit pin equal to it is redundant.

props.positive_test: returns a single parameter or prediction with no dispersion
props.examples: SGD-trained networks, OLS point estimates, k-means centroids

props.positive_test: returns an interval or decision with a stated long-run error rate
props.examples: bootstrap CIs, conformal intervals, confidence intervals, hypothesis tests

props.positive_test: returns or samples an explicit posterior over the model's parameters or latent functions
props.negative_test: returns an empirical spread across runs
props.examples: GP posteriors, MCMC samples, variational posteriors, SWAG, Bayesian NN
props.notes: narrowed to parameters and functions, which is what its test already said. A VAE's q(z|x) is a posterior over per-example latents while its weights are a point estimate, so phase 1's own VAE worked example failed this test -- that case is A.uncert.latent

props.positive_test: infers a distribution over a per-example latent variable, while the parameters themselves stay a point estimate
props.negative_test: a posterior over parameters or functions (A.uncert.post); a predictive distribution over outputs (A.uncert.pred)
props.examples: VAE q(z|x), amortised inference networks, IAF posteriors, deep latent-variable models
props.notes: added after pinning: 42 A.uncert cases needed two values, and this conflation is why rather than genuine multi-valuedness

props.positive_test: returns a calibrated distribution or interval over the output for a new input, without representing uncertainty about the parameters
props.negative_test: a frequentist interval on a parameter (A.uncert.interval); a posterior over parameters (A.uncert.post)
props.examples: temperature scaling, Platt scaling, conformal prediction intervals, quantile regression outputs
props.notes: added after pinning: the whole L.calib.post branch had no value, and interval/point both misdescribe it

props.positive_test: expresses uncertainty as disagreement among independently obtained predictors
props.negative_test: expresses it through an explicit posterior
props.examples: deep ensembles, bagging variance, MC dropout as approximation, snapshot ensembles

props.scope: when the method is accompanied by a theorem
props.characteristic: what kind of mathematical statement the method comes with
props.positive_test: name the value this procedure takes for: formal guarantee claimed
props.examples: convergence, regret, consistency, coverage, certification, approximation, unbiasedness
props.notes: multi-valued cardinality=many from 14 pinning cases: genuine: one theorem can prove consistency and unbiasedness no default on purpose: an empty A.guar means no theorem is claimed, which is informative -- the whole generative region being empty was reported as a finding, not a gap

props.positive_test: proves convergence to a stationary or optimal point under stated conditions
props.examples: FISTA rates, SVRG rates, convex SGD rates, ADMM convergence

props.positive_test: bounds cumulative loss relative to the best fixed or dynamic comparator
props.examples: UCB1, EXP3, LinUCB, online mirror descent, Thompson-sampling regret

props.positive_test: proves the estimate converges to the truth as sample size grows
props.examples: MLE consistency, doubly robust estimators, TMLE, double ML, M-estimation theory
props.notes: the main guarantee in the causal branch

props.positive_test: guarantees a stated coverage probability at finite sample size
props.examples: split conformal prediction, conformal risk control, distribution-free intervals

props.positive_test: proves invariance of the prediction within a stated input region
props.examples: randomised smoothing, IBP, CROWN, convex relaxations

props.positive_test: proves a bounded ratio to the optimum of a hard combinatorial objective
props.negative_test: proves no bound on solution quality
props.examples: greedy submodular 1-1/e, k-means++ expected ratio, k-center greedy

props.positive_test: the estimator's expectation equals the target quantity
props.negative_test: the estimator is biased but lower variance
props.examples: REINFORCE score-function estimator, IPS, Horvitz-Thompson, unbiased MLMC
props.notes: often the explicit selling point over a biased rival

props.scope: to every algorithm
props.characteristic: what artifact, if any, survives the run
props.positive_test: name the value this procedure takes for: separable-model production
props.examples: parametric, instance-based, transductive
props.notes: single-valued cardinality=many from 25 pinning cases: genuine: RAG, kNN-LM, ProtoNets and iCaRL all ship parameters AND need stored instances at prediction time. Still missing A.param.none -- it claims universal scope and is blank on 168 nodes in one region alone default=A.param.param: emitting parameters is the unmarked case. A blank means the default, so an explicit pin equal to it is redundant.

props.positive_test: emits a fixed-size parameter set runnable on new inputs without the training data
props.negative_test: needs the training data at prediction time
props.examples: SGD-trained networks, OLS coefficients, GMM parameters, random forests
props.notes: the models dimension has an entry

A.param.inst.name: Keeps the data as the model

props.positive_test: prediction requires the stored training examples themselves
props.examples: k-NN, kernel SVM support vectors, KDE, LOESS, Gaussian processes
props.notes: the legal "algorithm with no model" case

props.positive_test: produces an output only for the points it was given; new points need a refit
props.negative_test: produces a map applicable to unseen points
props.examples: t-SNE, spectral clustering, DBSCAN, label propagation, MDS, UMAP-without-transform
props.notes: the second legal "no model" case

props.positive_test: the run leaves behind nothing that could be applied to anything -- it emits an output and the procedure is over
props.negative_test: anything that emits parameters, keeps data as the model, or produces a transductive result that is itself the output
props.examples: beam search, a diffusion solver, an optimiser step rule, gradient checkpointing
props.notes: added after pinning: A.param declares scope `applies to every algorithm` and was blank on 168 nodes in one region and all 308 in another, so its own scope was false

props.scope: to every procedure that reorganises or distributes an existing computation

props.positive_test: name the value this procedure takes for: function preservation

A blank means the default, so an explicit pin equal to it is redundant.

props.positive_test: produces the same result as the unreorganised computation, up to floating-point reassociation

props.positive_test: changes the result by a bounded or controlled amount
props.examples: mixed precision, post-training quantization, gradient compression

props.positive_test: changes the trajectory the run follows, so the learned object differs
props.examples: FedAvg, local SGD, asynchronous updates

props.scope: to any procedure whose output has more than one element scored together

props.negative_test: a single independent prediction per input, which is A.outstruct.atomic

A blank means the default, so an explicit pin equal to it is redundant.

props.positive_test: each output element is predicted and scored independently of the others

props.positive_test: the output is an ordered sequence scored jointly across positions

A blank means the default, so an explicit pin equal to it is redundant.

props.positive_test: all training data belongs to one party, however many devices it is spread over
props.examples: ordinary data-parallel training, ZeRO, Megatron

props.positive_test: very many intermittently available clients, each holding little data
props.examples: federated learning on phones, FedAvg as originally posed, FedBuff

props.positive_test: a small number of persistent organisational parties, each holding a substantial dataset

props.scope: to every procedure that repeats a step

props.positive_test: reaches its answer in one solve and stops

props.positive_test: repeats a map until the iterate stops moving, by a tolerance or until no assignment changes
